intro: If you're coming to work, handle business, or stop over for a night around Laem Chabang Seaport and the industrial estate in the Si Racha area, and you want a clean, quiet room with easy parking at a price that won't hurt — NYTH Hotel - Laem Chabang Seaport is a name people around here bring up often · It's a small 3-star boutique hotel of about 50 rooms in Thung Sukhla sub-district, Si Racha, that leans on peace and quiet, clean minimalist rooms, and a location close to the port and the industrial estate rather than being a beachfront resort like the ones in Bang Saen or Pattaya · There's no swimming pool and it isn't on the beach, but it gives you a good-value room, service many guests praise, and the convenience that matters if you're here for work or passing through · Prices start at about ฿545/night · scored 8.0 from 402 reviews on Agoda and 8.4 on Trip.com

body.html: Overview and who it's for — if you had to sum this place up in one sentence, NYTH Hotel - Laem Chabang Seaport is "a hotel for people who have a reason to be around Laem Chabang" rather than a place to stay for a seaside holiday · It's a small 3-star boutique hotel with about 50 rooms, set in Thung Sukhla sub-district, Si Racha, Chonburi, in an area surrounded by Laem Chabang Seaport, the industrial estate, and the Space Krenovation Park · The hotel positions itself as a "chic hotel" near the port, with the emphasis on clean, good-looking rooms, easy-to-reach prices, and a quiet setting · From sifting through real guest reviews, the people it suits best are business travellers and staff coming to work or attend meetings around the Laem Chabang industrial estate, truck drivers or people working with the port, crew members stopping over before boarding, and travellers driving through who just want a place to sleep for a night at a budget price · On the flip side, if you're after sea views, a swimming pool, a sandy beach to stroll along, or a resort atmosphere for a holiday, this isn't the answer, and you should look toward Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · Put simply, NYTH sells clean, quiet, good value and a location near where the work is, not luxury or a holiday vibe

Location and getting around — NYTH sits at 99/99 Moo 9, Nong Rae Road, Thung Sukhla sub-district, Si Racha, an area tied to the industrial and logistics economy of Chonburi's eastern side · The strength of this location is that it's close to Laem Chabang Seaport and the Laem Chabang Industrial Estate, just a few minutes' drive away, which makes it very convenient for people here on business · The Space Krenovation Park is only about a 4 min drive away, and the industrial estate is within about 5 min · Nearby temples and parks such as Wat Prachakhom Wanaram, Wat Manorom, and Laem Chabang Public Park are about 1–1.3 km away · Pattaya Beach, the main tourist draw, is about 21 km away, or roughly a 30 min drive · One thing that has to be said plainly, straight from real reviews, is that this location is fairly quiet and about 500 metres from restaurants and convenience stores — there's no cluster of food and shops right outside the hotel like you'd get in a town centre · Anyone driving their own car will have the easiest time, since parking is free, while those without a car should plan ahead for getting to food or into central Si Racha, which may mean relying on a taxi or a ride-hailing app that can be harder to book at certain times than in the city

"Clean room, comfortable bed, very quiet, slept soundly all night. Great location near my workplace in the industrial estate, just a few minutes' drive. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the price was worth what you get. If I'm working around Laem Chabang again I'll definitely come back."

Room types and decor — the rooms at NYTH lean toward simple, contemporary minimalist style; not luxurious, but clean-looking and with more design sense than the average budget hotel · The main rooms break down into the Economy King Bed Room, the compact entry-level room, and the Superior King Bed Room at around 24 sqm, which is a bit larger and slightly better appointed, mostly on floors 1–3 of the building · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, free Wi-Fi, and a private bathroom · What the hotel highlights as a selling point is its ozone room-cleaning service (Ozone Cleaning Room), which helps with cleanliness and odour and is a touch that many guests feel goes beyond what they paid · Most real reviews praise the rooms as clean, the beds as comfortable, the setting as quiet, and the decor as nicer than the price suggests · But there are honest caveats worth knowing — some reviews feel parts of the rooms and building are starting to show their age and look a bit worn from use, some room fittings are getting tired, and cleanliness standards may not be consistent across every room and every visit, so set your expectations at the level of a clean, quiet budget hotel rather than a brand-new one

Facilities and the pool question — this has to be made clear from the start because it's the thing people ask about most — NYTH currently has no swimming pool in service · Some listings on booking sites still say there's a pool, but many recent real reviews agree that the pool is no longer open, so if you're coming specifically for a pool, drop it from your expectations and confirm directly with the hotel before booking · The facilities that do exist lean toward a convenient stopover hotel rather than a resort — there's a restaurant open for lunch and dinner, room service, laundry and dry-cleaning, luggage storage, free Wi-Fi throughout, and free parking, which helps a lot if you're driving your own car · There's a small garden on the grounds where you can sit and get some air, and the hotel also offers tour and ticket booking for those who want to continue on to Pattaya or elsewhere · The real selling point here isn't the number of facilities, but the cleanliness, the quiet, and the easy parking at a budget price, which matches what the core group of guests coming for work actually want

Food and the restaurant — NYTH has an in-house restaurant open for lunch and dinner, which helps a lot because the location is fairly quiet and the nearest outside restaurants are about 500 metres away · At times the hotel serves breakfast, and there are older reviews that mention breakfast with an organic-vegetable salad bar in a garden setting, a detail some guests were impressed by · That said, to be straight with you, the breakfast details and menu may change depending on the season and the room type you book, and some budget packages may not include breakfast, so check the conditions clearly when you book · For other meals, anyone with a car can head out to à la carte restaurants, seafood places, and convenience stores in Thung Sukhla and central Si Racha, which aren't far, including local specialities like Si Racha seafood and seaside seafood spots that are a short drive away · Overall, food isn't a reason to come to NYTH for the in-house dining, but having a restaurant and room service helps with convenience for someone who's worn out from work and doesn't want to go anywhere at night

Service and staff — service is where NYTH earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews, and it's one reason the overall score still sits at a good level · Many guests say the staff are friendly, attentive, and willing to help, and some older reviews even recount management going beyond expectations to arrange tours and transport · For guests here on business and tired from travelling, finding a team that checks you in quickly and is ready to help is genuinely valuable · But for balance, it has to be said honestly that there have been some past comments about being charged a price at the counter that differed from the price booked online, which is the key reason we recommend booking through an online platform and keeping proof of your booking and the confirmed price for peace of mind · Overall, service is still a strength here, and it's a part that helps lift the whole experience even when the building itself isn't new

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together from Agoda, Trip.com, Tripadvisor, and various review sources, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: rooms that are clean and very quiet with comfortable beds for a sound sleep, minimalist decor that looks nicer than the price, a location near the port and the industrial estate that's convenient for workers, friendly and helpful staff, free and roomy parking, and very good value especially when booked online · Many guests here for work say they'll come back when they're in the area · On the caveat side: the most talked-about issue is that there's no longer a pool even though some listings still say there is, which leaves people who expected one disappointed · Next is that parts of the building and rooms are starting to age and cleanliness standards aren't consistent, with some past reviews even seeing it as old and worn · On top of that there's the location being about 500 metres from restaurants and too quiet for anyone who wants some buzz, and the matter of counter pricing differing from online prices in some cases · Most of these gripes can be managed by setting the right expectations, booking online, and confirming details with the hotel beforehand, rather than being deal-breakers that make a stay impossible

"Great value if you book online. The rooms are simple, clean and have some design to them, in a quiet area, good for people coming to work · The only downsides are there's no pool anymore even though some places still list one, and the restaurants are a bit far so you need to drive. But if you're staying for work, it's worth it for both the price and the cleanliness."

Price comparison and value — nightly room rates start at about ฿545/night for an Economy room on weekdays when booked online, and climb to around ฿700–฿1,200 for a Superior room or during periods with events or festivals around Laem Chabang · What makes NYTH good value is that you get a clean, design-conscious room, a quiet setting, free parking, and a location near where the work is, at a price far below the big chain hotels in the same area · Compared with an upmarket hotel in Laem Chabang–Si Racha such as the Holiday Inn & Suites Siracha Laemchabang, which has a pool and full facilities but costs several times more, NYTH loses on facilities and newness but wins clearly on price and value for someone who just needs a clean bed near work · And compared with other budget stays around Laem Chabang that also start at about 550 baht, NYTH usually has the edge on room design and higher review scores · In short, if you weight price, cleanliness, and a location near the port and the industrial estate, every baht you pay feels well returned

Things to know before booking — there are a few things that make a stay smoother · One, there's currently no swimming pool, even though some booking-site listings still say there is, so if that matters to you, confirm directly with the hotel first · Two, you should book through an online platform and keep proof of the confirmed price, because there are past reviews mentioning counter pricing that differed from online · Three, the location is fairly quiet and about 500 metres from restaurants, so if you don't have a car, plan ahead for getting to food or use the hotel's room service / restaurant · Four, set your expectations at the level of a clean, quiet budget hotel, not a resort or a new hotel, because parts of the building and rooms are starting to age · Five, if you're mainly here to visit Pattaya, this location is about a 30 min drive away, so weigh whether it's worth it for the saving on the room, or choose to stay closer to the attractions instead · Six, during periods with events or activities in the industrial estate, rooms can fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms

The verdict — from everything real reviews say, NYTH Hotel - Laem Chabang Seaport is the place that suits best for people coming for work or passing through the Laem Chabang–Si Racha area who want a clean, quiet room with easy parking at a budget price · The cleanliness of the rooms, the quiet, the design that looks nicer than the price, the friendly service, and the location near the port and the industrial estate make it worthwhile for business travellers, staff, truck drivers, crew members, and travellers who just need a good bed for one night · But you have to accept, honestly, that there's no longer a pool, it isn't on the beach, the location is fairly quiet and far from restaurants, parts of the building are starting to age, and there have been past issues with counter pricing · If you're looking for a resort with a pool, sea views, or a holiday atmosphere, this isn't the answer, and you should look at options on the Bang Saen or Pattaya side instead · But for a practical stay — coming for work or stopping over for a night around Laem Chabang — where you want cleanliness and value on a tight budget, NYTH meets that need well, and it's the reason it has kept a good review score in this area for so long

faq.q: Where is NYTH Hotel · how close is it to Laem Chabang Seaport?
faq.a: NYTH is at 99/99 Moo 9, Nong Rae Road, Thung Sukhla sub-district, Si Racha, Chonburi · It's close to Laem Chabang Seaport and the Laem Chabang Industrial Estate, just a few minutes' drive away · The Space Krenovation Park is about a 4 min drive · Nearby temples and parks are about 1–1.3 km away · Pattaya Beach is about 21 km away, or roughly a 30 min drive

faq.q: Does NYTH Hotel have a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's currently no swimming pool in service · Even though some booking-site listings still say there's a pool, recent real reviews agree that the pool is no longer open · If a pool matters to you, confirm directly with the hotel before booking, or choose a place with a pool in the Bang Saen or Pattaya area instead

faq.q: What's the starting price at NYTH Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿545/night for an Economy King room when booked online on a weekday · The Superior King room of around 24 sqm is about ฿790 and up · Some packages include breakfast (check the conditions when booking) · We recommend booking through an online platform, since prices are usually better than at the counter, and compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is NYTH Hotel best suited to?
faq.a: It's very well suited to business travellers, staff coming to work or attend meetings around the Laem Chabang industrial estate, people working with the port, crew members, and travellers driving through who want a clean, quiet place to sleep at a budget price · It isn't suited to people who want a resort with a swimming pool, sea views, or a holiday atmosphere, who should consider the Bang Saen or Pattaya side instead

faq.q: Does NYTH Hotel have food and parking?
faq.a: Yes · the hotel has a restaurant open for lunch and dinner and room service, which helps a lot because the nearest outside restaurants are about 500 metres away · Some packages include breakfast (older reviews mention an organic-vegetable salad bar in the garden) · There's free parking and free Wi-Fi throughout, good for people driving their own car

faq.q: Is it easy to get to NYTH Hotel without a car?
faq.a: The location is in an area that's fairly quiet and about 500 metres from restaurants and convenience stores, so without your own car, getting to food or into central Si Racha is harder than in a town-centre area · There's free parking for those who drive · People without a car should plan to use the hotel's restaurant and room service, or a ride-hailing app, which can be harder to book at certain times than in the city
